judged_text: The webhook's update path replaces the entire Credential.key JSON with the decrypted payload (`data: { key: keys }`) without validating the object against the app's credential schema and without preserving or backing up the previous value. A self-hosted user who had already personally connected the same app silently loses their existing OAuth grant/tokens the first time the parent instance pushes credentials — the pre-existing key is destroyed and unrecoverable, so disabling credential sharing later leaves those users with no working connection and no rollback short of re-authenticating every user; additionally any valid-JSON-but-wrong-shape payload from the parent (e.g. {} or a shape from a mismatched app version) is persisted as the user's credential with no validation error, breaking the integration.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the decrypted payload is blindly `JSON.parse`d and then persisted as the credential key. On update it overwrites the entire stored JSON (`prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: keys } })`) for the first matching credential (by `userId` + `appId`) with no validation against any app-specific credential schema and no attempt to preserve/merge prior fields. This makes it possible to persist valid-JSON but wrong-shape payloads (e.g., `{}`) and to destroy a user’s previously stored OAuth tokens/fields for that app when a webhook arrives.
